scripts.clear: gjsify clear lib tsconfig.tsbuildinfo tsconfig.types.tsbuildinfo test.gjs.mjs test.node.mjs
scripts.build: gjsify run build:gjsify && gjsify run build:types
scripts.build:test: gjsify run build:test:gjs && gjsify run build:test:node
scripts.test: gjsify run build:gjsify && gjsify run build:test && gjsify run test:node && gjsify run test:gjs

osNotes.darwin: `os.cpus()` reports the documented all-zero `times` on macOS. Linux reads the per-CPU tick counters from `/proc/stat`; the darwin equivalent is Mach’s `host_processor_info(PROCESSOR_CPU_LOAD_INFO)`, which GJS cannot call without a native bridge, and no userland tool prints the cumulative per-core totals Node returns (`top`/`iostat` give an instantaneous aggregate percentage). Every other export — cpus model/speed, memory, uptime, loadavg, networkInterfaces, userInfo — is real on darwin and covered by the macOS suites. `src/index.spec.ts` carries the matching `it.failing(…, { when })`, so the claim retires itself the day a reader exists. `os.constants.signals` was a Linux table served to every host until #2001 and is now XNU’s (`src/signals.ts`): its darwin table is asserted key-for-key by `src/signals.spec.ts` on Linux AND against native Node by `macos-suites.yml`, so those numbers are measured rather than claimed. What is left in this claim is the `cpus()` gap alone.
osNotes.win32: A `src/win32.ts` covers the per-platform answers, but it is unexercised for the same structural reason as `@gjsify/child_process`: `runtimes.node: "none"` sends `test:node` to native Node, and there is no GJS host on Windows to run `test:gjs`. Measured on the win11-gjsify VM: 10 of 178 specs fail there, and all ten are POSIX assumptions in the SPECS (asserting `type()` is `Linux`, EOL is `\n`, devNull is `/dev/null`) rather than defects in this module. Two things now differ from that shape. `os.constants.signals` is NOT unexercised: `windows-suites.yml` runs `test:node`, whose `on(‘Node.js’)` block compares our win32 table against native Node’s on a real Windows host (#2001), so those seven CRT numbers are verified there rather than asserted from Linux. The SELECTION is still unexercised — `src/signals.ts` picks the table from `getOs()`’s `uname` probe, which no GJS host on Windows has ever run, because none exists (ADR 0024 § 4). `os.constants.errno` and `dlopen` remain glibc’s on this host too; see `status/open-todos/runtime-apis.md`.
